source.title: Many-Shot In-Context Learning
source.authors: Rishabh Agarwal; Avi Singh; Lei M. Zhang; Bernd Bohnet; Stephanie Chan; Biao Zhang; Ankesh Anand; Zaheer Abbas; Azade Nova; John D. Co-Reyes; Eric Chu; Feryal M. P. Behbahani; Aleksandra Faust; H. Larochelle

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether next-token loss predicts downstream ICL performance and reports cases where the loss trend does not track task performance. It does not test parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling power laws.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are in §4.8 and Figure 18, with task-performance comparisons in Figures 7 and 8. The measured NLL is conditional on many-shot prompts, not held-out pretraining loss; the paper does not sweep model parameters, training tokens, or training compute. Other many-shot ICL results do not bear on the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: No claim version is tested. The study varies the number of in-context shots for one fixed model (Gemini 1.5 Pro) and compares prompt-conditioned NLL on ground-truth test solutions with task accuracy. It does not vary parameters, training tokens or compute, and does not measure held-out pretraining loss. V6 concerns downstream performance tracking model scale or pretraining loss. A 'long-context scaling law' over shots for one model is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version. Kaplan et al. is cited only as one of the prior works on long-context loss trends.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state they confirm that ground-truth NLL falls predictably with context length, as long-context scaling laws report. Their claim is that this NLL trend is not a reliable proxy for ICL performance on problem-solving tasks. They do not claim anything about pretraining-loss scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies in-context example count and measures prompt-conditioned test NLL and task performance; it does not reproduce the original training-scaling or compute-allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and ICL prompt regime affect the relationship: MATH and GPQA task performance falls after its peak without a matching NLL increase, while GSM8K transfer performance improves with little NLL change. The paper also says NLL curves for reinforced and unsupervised ICL generally have smaller slopes than supervised ICL.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemini 1.5 Pro, NLL on ground-truth test solutions decreases as shot count grows for MATH and GPQA. Task accuracy nonetheless peaks near 125 shots and then declines. GSM8K transfer accuracy improves while NLL barely changes. NLL with ground-truth demonstrations is lower than with model-generated ones, even though model-generated ones often perform better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-length (many-shot) NLL scaling within one model does not reliably predict in-context-learning task performance on reasoning tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2024, Spotlight Presentation
record.problems: The relevant loss is prompt-conditioned test NLL rather than pretraining loss. The NLL and performance trends are presented in figures without numerical values in the text, and the tested model is Gemini 1.5 Pro. The paper notes that the absolute NLL for ICL and unsupervised ICL is not directly comparable because their prompt formats differ.
record.rows_left_out: Other many-shot task-performance results, including translation, summarization, planning, verifier, reasoning, sentiment, and synthetic-function experiments, do not measure the listed scaling-law versions. Figure 18’s additional reinforced/unsupervised NLL curves are discussed qualitatively but do not add a separate explicit loss-versus-task-performance result to the comparisons extracted here.

untested.parts: Power-law pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of power-law fits from small to large training runs.
Compute-optimal split between parameters and tokens.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power laws in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream performance versus model scale or pretraining loss. Only in-context NLL versus shots for a single model is studied.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5/V6 challenges' verdict conflates in-context shot scaling with model scale or pretraining-loss scaling. The only model-size comparison is a qualitative one between Gemini 1.5 Pro and 1.5 Flash on translation (§4.5). It reports no loss and no scaling fit, so it does not bear on V6 either.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of power-law fits from small training runs to larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss forms in other modalities or training regimes.
Pretraining loss and model-scale effects are not tested; the study evaluates prompt-conditioned NLL versus ICL task performance as the number of in-context examples changes.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices or training setup.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: MATH and GPQA ICL; GSM8K transfer
reader_labels.reason: Task performance declines on MATH and GPQA without a corresponding NLL increase, and GSM8K transfer performance improves while NLL changes close to nil (r1–r6). This challenges loss-based downstream predictability in these tested ICL settings.
